anomalies.observed: R29 10k connects the gate node of ATO-valve MOSFET T7 to GND, and T1 is an NPN common-emitter stage that can only pull that same gate node low.
anomalies.expected: The gate needs a pull-up to +3V3, as in the main-pump driver where R45 10k pulls the gate high, so the NPN can pull it low to turn off and release it high to turn on. The specification describes the ATO valve as a low-side switch driven through a BT3904 pre-driver.

evidence.quote: R29 10k, T1 BT3904, T7 AO3400A in the MAIN PUMP & VALVE DRIVERS sheet
T3 — AON6407 (DPAK N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).

anomalies.impact: The ATO valve gate is held low and can never be driven high, so the ATO solenoid valve never energizes and automatic top-off cannot open the fill valve.

anomalies.observed: T5 is marked AON6407 and is placed in series in the high-side 24 V input path; R40/D4 form a gate network referenced to ground, which is a P-channel high-side reverse-polarity-protection arrangement.
anomalies.expected: A P-channel MOSFET, or a proper N-channel ideal-diode/charge-pump controller, is required for this high-side reverse-polarity topology. The specification identifies AON6407 as an N-channel MOSFET used for low-side switching, not for this high-side gate-to-ground arrangement.

evidence.quote: T5 AON6407 in the POWER TRAIN sheet, under the label Reverse polarity protection
T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch

anomalies.impact: The N-channel device will not enhance in this high-side gate-to-ground circuit. It may conduct only through its body diode, giving a large voltage drop and heating, or fail to pass 24 V, so the board may not power reliably.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains two functional errors: the ATO valve gate is tied low and cannot be turned on, and the 24 V high-side reverse-polarity pass device uses an N-channel MOSFET where a P-channel or ideal-diode arrangement is required.
